chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:

ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: “If the nose of a slave and his male organ are cut off, or something is done that amounts to his full value, the value of the slave is paid to his master, and the slave is taken.”

key_terms.أَنْفُ: the nose, mentioned as a specific bodily organ whose severance is legally consequential
key_terms.أُخِذَ الْعَبْدُ: the slave is taken, indicating transfer under the legal consequence described
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave, the injured person whose legal valuation is under discussion
key_terms.ذَكَرُهُ: his male organ, mentioned as a severe bodily injury in the ruling
key_terms.قِيمَةُ الْعَبْدِ: the full value of the slave, the amount due in compensation
key_terms.قِيمَتِهِ: his monetary value, the financial measure used in determining liability
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, the legal owner to whom the compensation is paid

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave suffers an injury equal to his full value?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding injury inflicted upon a slave when the injury reaches the equivalent of the slave’s full monetary value. In such a case, the slave’s value is paid to his master, and the slave is then taken by the one liable under the ruling.
